div.head: Leis Wl 10.1
div.ab: De sa[r]bote, ceo est de la dulur: Si la plaie lui vient el vis en descuvert, al pouz tuteveies VIII den.; u en la teste u en auter liu, u ele seit cuverte: al pouz tuteveies IIII den. E de tanz os cum l’om trait de la plaie, al os tuteveies IIII den.

De sarbote, cho est de la dulor: Si la plaie lui vient a vis en descuvert, al polz toteveie . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . IIII den. Et de tanz os cum hom trarad de la plaie, al os toteveie IIII den.
Deinde si plaga in discooperto faciei fuerit, semper ad unciam . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . IIII den. persoluet. Et si ossa abstracta, quot ossa, tociens IIII d. dabit.

De sa[r]bote, ceo est de la dulur:—Si la plaie lui vient el vis en descuvert, al pouz tuteveies VIII den., u en la teste u en auter liu u ele seit cuverte, al puoz tuteveies IIII den. E de tanz os cum l'om trait de la plaie al os tuteveies IIII den.

10, 1. Von Wundenbusse, d. h. für den Schmerz: Wenn die Wunde ihm ins Gesicht, in Unbedecktes kommt, für [je]den Zoll immer 8 Pfennig; oder [wenn] auf den Kopf oder an eine andere Stelle, wo sie [die Narbe] bedeckt ist: für [je]den Zoll immer 4 Pfennig. Und für so viele Knochen[splitter], wie man aus der Wunde zieht, für [je]den Knochen immer 4 Pfennig.

10, 1. Of wound-compensation, i.e. for the pain: if the wound comes in his face, on an uncovered part, for [ea]ch inch always 8 pennies; or [if] on the head or in another place where it [the scar] is covered: for [ea]ch inch always 4 pennies. And for as many bone[-splinters] as are drawn from the wound, for [ea]ch bone always 4 pennies.

With regard to sarbot, that is [compensation] for a wound:—If he is wounded on the face, on a part which is visible, for every inch 8 pence shall be paid in every case; if on the head or in any other place where it is hidden, for every inch 4 pence shall be paid in every case. And for every piece of bone drawn out of the wound 4 pence shall be paid in every case.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 258–259 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text and German translation added from Gesetze I p. 500–501, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

Das Kompositum sarbot zitiert Toller nur hierher. Der Zusammenhang erfordert ‘Wundenbusse’; Agsächs. heisst aber sar (s. Wb) ‘Schmerz, Leiden’, wie auch F übersetzt, nicht ‘Wunde’. Daher erklärt Steenstrup (Danelag 315) das Wort aus Nord. sarbætr. Doch übs. Sweet sar auch ‘Wunde’, und diese Bed. ist Mittelenglisch bezeugt

Toller cites the compound sarbot only from this passage. The context requires ‘compensation for wounds’; in A.-S., however, sar (see Wb) means ‘pain, suffering’, as F also translates, not ‘wound’. Steenstrup (Danelag 315) therefore explains the word from Norse sarbætr. Sweet, however, also translates sar as ‘wound’, and this meaning is attested in Middle English
